This isn't as pretty as I would like, but here's the working spec:

```python
(
        T.items(), 
        Iter(
          (A.globals.gp_item, T[1].values(), 
           Iter({'val': 'c', 
                 'path': S.globals.gp_item[0]}))
        ).flatten().all()
)
```

And I get:
```
[
    {
        "val": 1,
        "path": "a"
    }
]
```


[Here's a link to a glompad where you can fool around with it in your browser](https://yak.party/glompad/#spec=%28%0A++++T.items%28%29%2C%0A++++Iter%28%0A++++++++%28%0A++++++++++++A.globals.gp_item%2C%0A++++++++++++T%5B1%5D.values%28%29%2C%0A++++++++++++%5B%7B%22val%22%3A+%22c%22%2C+%22path%22%3A+S.globals.gp_item%5B0%5D%7D%5D%2C%0A++++++++%29%0A++++%29%0A++++.flatten%28%29%0A++++.all%28%29%2C%0A%29%0A&target=%7B%0A++%22a%22%3A+%7B%0A++++%22b%22%3A+%7B%0A++++++%22c%22%3A+1%0A++++%7D%0A++%7D%0A%7D&v=1).

Two key things to note:

* I'm using [the `globals` member](https://glom.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#sensible-saving-vars-s-globals) of the scope (and [the `A` assignment shortcut](https://glom.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#updating-the-scope-s-a)) to save the grandparent item before we descend. Probably when you used `S` the value was being lost because the scope was local.
    * If this is part of a much larger spec, you can create your own non-local, non-global scope with `Vars` documented in the link above.
    * I found it simpler to save the grandparent item (key and value), instead of just the value, and then only emit the key (`gp_item[0]`).
*  Notice I'm using two `Iter` specs. glom doesn't yet have full tree traversal, so the nesting of the spec is going to roughly match the nesting of your data. If you need this to work in an arbitrary nested structure, I recommend [`remap`](https://sedimental.org/remap.html), the recursive map function, part of [`boltons.iterutils`](https://boltons.readthedocs.io/en/latest/iterutils.html#nested). 

Hope this
